string.text: Planned: new combat actions the vanilla planner lacks, melee first. Nothing to configure yet.

Stalkers stand their ground instead of jogging to new cover mid-exchange. A stalker who sees his target with a clear shot keeps fighting from where he stands; losing the target or the time limit below lets the cover move through again. Requires a recent engine build with the action-switch veto; on older builds the toggle has no effect and vanilla behavior applies.

Stalker rank decides how tightly a stalker's gun tracks you while you move, how far it leads you, and how fast you are noticed at range. Tracking speed changes their gun handling on a moving target; it does not make the first shot come sooner. Requires a recent engine build with the per-stalker aim and vision binds; on older builds the page has no effect and vanilla behavior applies.

Planned: engagement distance. The game stops NPC fights at a hard range cap regardless of weapon, so a sniper never fires at the distances his rifle exists for, and a stalker sniped from beyond the cap can duck (the Danger hit response) but never answer. This page will let long-range NPCs answer and initiate at their weapon's real reach. Nothing to configure yet.
Planned: NPC toughness from what they carry - armor and equipment, damage mitigators, and artefacts. Nothing to configure yet.
Planned: player-facing combat feedback, concussion first. Nothing to configure yet.
Planned: mutant combat behavior. Nothing to configure yet.

Wound one member of a squad and the whole squad learns the shooter at once, including patrol members out of earshot and against a suppressed weapon. Vanilla shares only a shooter the squadmates heard. AlifeTactics enables the shooter in every member's memory and registers the squad into combat, then the engine's own propagation carries it. No relations are faked. The survivor gate below keeps a clean instant kill quiet, and the squad can still find the body.
When off, vanilla behavior runs unmodified: squadmates learn about a shooter only within earshot, and distant patrol members never do.

When the hit kills the victim outright, the shooter is not disclosed. The dying man never gets to radio it in, so silenced shots and backstabs stay quiet. The squad can still find you the honest way: by sound, by sight, or by the body. A hit that only wounds discloses as usual.
Game minutes without new hits before a squad forgets a shooter. The next hit re-fires the full-squad alert. Game time, not real time.

Wounded stalkers heal with the medkits and bandages they carry, and you can watch it: a hurt man limps, a healing man plays the gesture, out of combat only. Vanilla ships the healing item lists empty, so carried kits were never used and bleeders died with full pockets. AlifeTactics restores the lists at boot. Heal rate, the per-rank charge for empty pockets, and the animations tune below.

Master toggle for the runtime layer: heal rate scaling and the per-rank healing charge. When off, vanilla self-heal behavior runs unmodified. Restart required to toggle. The item-list restoration is boot-time and always active.
Scales how much health each self-heal tick restores. At 2.0 a medkit heals twice as fast, at 0.5 half as fast. The number of ticks is fixed by the engine.

Chance that a novice-rank stalker gets one lifetime healing charge at first spawn. The charge fires once when he drops below the heal threshold with no medkit in inventory. Vanilla rolls a flat 50% for every rank.

Out-of-combat stalkers below the health threshold visibly limp: a hurt idle while standing, a hurt walk while moving, matched to the carried weapon. Fighting stalkers are excluded so combat posture is never disrupted.
Health fraction below which an eligible stalker starts limping. Lower values delay the cue until he is more seriously hurt.
Plays a medkit or bandage gesture when a stalker starts a heal cycle, out of combat only. The engine clears it when the gesture ends.

Stalker accuracy scales with rank. A master shoots tighter than a novice, each tier tunable below. The engine has a per-rank dispersion curve, but Anomaly's rank values leave it flat, so every stalker fires with the same spread. AlifeTactics drives the curve through the engine's own dispersion callback. Weapon and barrel dispersion stay untouched. This scales the stalker's skill.
When off, the engine's flat dispersion applies to every stalker regardless of rank.
Shot cone scale for novice-rank stalkers. Lower is tighter and more lethal. 1.00 matches the vanilla cone.
Shot cone scale for trainee-rank stalkers. Lower is tighter.
Shot cone scale for experienced-rank stalkers. Lower is tighter.
Shot cone scale for professional-rank stalkers. Lower is tighter.
Shot cone scale for veteran-rank stalkers. Lower is tighter.
Shot cone scale for expert-rank stalkers. Lower is tighter.
Shot cone scale for master-rank stalkers. Lower is tighter.
Shot cone scale for legend-rank stalkers, the highest rank. Lower is tighter.
How much of the movement spread penalty a novice-rank stalker keeps while shooting on the move. 1.00 is the full vanilla penalty; lower is steadier fire on the move.
How much of the movement spread penalty a trainee-rank stalker keeps while shooting on the move. Lower is steadier.
How much of the movement spread penalty an experienced-rank stalker keeps while shooting on the move. Lower is steadier.
How much of the movement spread penalty a professional-rank stalker keeps while shooting on the move. Lower is steadier.
How much of the movement spread penalty a veteran-rank stalker keeps while shooting on the move. Lower is steadier.
How much of the movement spread penalty an expert-rank stalker keeps while shooting on the move. Lower is steadier.
How much of the movement spread penalty a master-rank stalker keeps while shooting on the move. Lower is steadier.
How much of the movement spread penalty a legend-rank stalker keeps while shooting on the move, the highest rank. 0.50 makes his moving fire as steady as his standing fire.
When off, every stalker aims and spots at the engine's flat speed regardless of rank.
How tightly a novice-rank barrel follows a moving target, radians per second. 0.24 matches the vanilla engine.
How tightly a trainee-rank barrel follows a moving target. Higher tracks closer.
How tightly a experienced-rank barrel follows a moving target. Higher tracks closer.
How tightly a professional-rank barrel follows a moving target. Higher tracks closer.
How tightly a veteran-rank barrel follows a moving target. Higher tracks closer.
How tightly a expert-rank barrel follows a moving target. Higher tracks closer.
How tightly a master-rank barrel follows a moving target. Higher tracks closer.
How tightly a legend-rank barrel follows a moving target, the highest rank. 2.50 matches the game's hardcore AI aim option.
Seconds a novice-rank stalker aims ahead of a moving target. Lower lands closer when the target changes direction. 0.40 is the vanilla lead.
Seconds a trainee-rank stalker aims ahead of a moving target. Lower lands closer when the target changes direction.
Seconds an experienced-rank stalker aims ahead of a moving target. Lower lands closer when the target changes direction.
Seconds a professional-rank stalker aims ahead of a moving target. Lower lands closer when the target changes direction.
Seconds a veteran-rank stalker aims ahead of a moving target. Lower lands closer when the target changes direction.
Seconds an expert-rank stalker aims ahead of a moving target. Lower lands closer when the target changes direction.
Seconds a master-rank stalker aims ahead of a moving target. Lower lands closer when the target changes direction.
Seconds a legend-rank stalker aims ahead of a moving target, the highest rank. Lower lands closer when the target changes direction. 0.28 matches the game's hardcore AI aim option.

Planned: how each rank works the trigger, through a new engine hook. Rookies clamp it and spray long climbing bursts, top ranks squeeze short settled groups and let the weapon come back down. Nothing to configure yet.
Detection speed factor for novice-rank stalkers. Higher notices targets faster at range; 1.00 leaves your setup's detection unchanged. Point-blank detection is unaffected.
Detection speed factor for trainee-rank stalkers. Higher notices targets faster at range.
Detection speed factor for experienced-rank stalkers. Higher notices targets faster at range.
Detection speed factor for professional-rank stalkers. Higher notices targets faster at range.
Detection speed factor for veteran-rank stalkers. Higher notices targets faster at range.
Detection speed factor for expert-rank stalkers. Higher notices targets faster at range.
Detection speed factor for master-rank stalkers. Higher notices targets faster at range.
Detection speed factor for legend-rank stalkers, the highest rank. Higher notices targets faster at range. 2.00 notices targets twice as fast as your setup's baseline.
When off, stalkers may abandon a live exchange for new cover the moment the engine re-scores its cover point.
Seconds of refused cover moves before re-evaluation is allowed through again. Losing sight of the target or losing the clear shot lets the move through earlier.

A maneuver is a complete takeover of one stalker for a few seconds. AlifeTactics drives him through one committed move and hands him back to the engine cleanly. Vanilla, or whatever AI overhaul you run, drives every fight the rest of the time. Maneuvers run only in fights you are part of; NPC-only fights stay fully vanilla. A maneuver fires when its problem is real and ends when it is solved, so pressing the same stalker keeps drawing the same answer. The decisions come out looking human. Nobody turns his back on a shooter, two men never take the same cover. The takeover overrides no combat scripts, so it layers over AI overhauls. Each maneuver below toggles on its own.
When off, AlifeTactics never touches combat and every fight runs on your existing AI. When on, it may briefly borrow a stalker for one maneuver.
When on, AlifeTactics never takes over your companions, so their follow and combat AI and your commands stay in control. Turn off to let it maneuver them too.
A stalker shooting a distant target while a hostile player stands at contact range turns and engages the closer threat instead of presenting his back.
An enemy closed inside the stalker's minimum weapon range. He backs out to his own distance, still firing, down a lane he checked is clear.
Badly hurt with the shooter still in reach, a stalker pulls back to cover behind him, still firing. The cover always grows the distance to the shooter, and two men never claim the same spot.
The last man of a broken squad routs to a distant friendly base, weapon slung. He waits for a lull in the shooting first. Cautious factions only, fanatics never break.
A marksman stuck in a standoff plants and takes precision shots. He only plants beyond his enemy's effective range, and never while taking fire or under your crosshair.

Same-faction fighters no longer cut each other down in a crossfire. A hit between two NPCs of the same faction deals reduced damage, set by the slider below. It keys on their actual relation, so genuinely hostile factions still trade full damage. Your own shots are never touched.
When off, vanilla friendly-fire damage applies in full.
How much damage a same-faction hit deals. 0.00 means teammates take no damage from each other. 1.00 is full vanilla damage.

Stalkers read danger and investigate the way the engine always meant them to. A set of always-on fixes clears crashes and misreads across the danger check and the corpse investigation. Detection distances come from your setup's danger config, AlifeTactics adds the reactions. It installs as a runtime patch onto whichever danger script your modpack ships, so it layers over AI overhauls instead of replacing the file. Three improvements toggle below.

Vanilla stalkers ignore distant shooters because a distance gate caps the response. With this on a direct hit always registers, so a sniped stalker at 200m turns and seeks cover instead of standing still.

Stalkers hearing gunfire from an ENEMY seek cover and adopt threat poses, no line of sight needed. Gunfire from neutral or friendly stalkers, including yours, does not alarm them - that is the engine's relation rule, same as vanilla. Vanilla does nothing on this danger type even for enemies. Reaction distance follows your setup's danger config.
Danger caused by you reads the separate actor tables where your setup's danger config differentiates them (some AI overhauls do). With a config that ships identical tables this has no effect.

1. Three danger categories read the wrong config rows through a name collision. Each now reads its own. 
2. A mutant corpse crashed the danger time check. 
3. A torn-down NPC reference crashed the danger evaluator. 
4. A bad danger time value crashed the evaluator. 
5. The hit callback corrupted the danger memory with a missing shooter on every hit. 
6. Danger transitions left a stale lower-body animation playing. 
7. Leaving the danger state wiped every stalker's cover reservation instead of only its own. 
8. A corpse despawning mid-investigation crashed the investigator. 
9. The corpse investigation drove the wrong squad member through its stages. 
10. The investigator walked to a cleared spot instead of the cover it had found. 
11. The danger check re-parsed the same config strings on every evaluation. They parse once now (performance). 
12. A dead stalker's scripted danger no longer lingers on its id, so a respawn reusing the id starts clean. 
13. The corpse reaction crashed the game when it fired before its investigation stage was set.

NPC weapons jam only for real, and reload only when the magazine is spent. On modded exes every NPC rolls a fake per-rank jam from ammo spent, so even a full-condition rifle chokes and reloads every few rounds, and Anomaly has no jam animation to show it. AlifeTactics turns that roll off for NPCs. Your own jams stay vanilla.
On: NPC weapons never jam from the modded-exes roll. Off: the modded-exes default runs. Your own weapon jams are unaffected either way.

Stalkers fire the ammunition they actually carry. Veteran-rank and higher use the armor-piercing rounds from their own inventory, with real ballistics, and revert to standard rounds when the supply runs out. Each fight has a chance to consume one carried AP box, and faster weapons and lower ranks burn it sooner. The AP comes from the world through trade and looting, so what a stalker scavenged shapes how dangerous he is, and he drops none of it as loot. Rank threshold and drain rate tune in configs/alifetactics/at_ammo.ltx.
On: eligible stalkers load the AP they carry and spend it per fight. Off: every stalker fires vanilla standard rounds and no carried ammo is consumed.

Debug and development tools. DEBUG log level traces every system with timings: maneuver decisions, danger evaluation, disclosure, healing ticks and consumed items, per-shot accuracy, ammo and reload events. Written to alifetactics.log. Tracing has a cost, leave at WARN for normal play.
Log verbosity. ERROR: failures only. WARN: anomalies. INFO: module init and patch installs. DEBUG: full per-event tracing with durations.

Live overlay of nearby stalkers: rank and name, health, logic scheme, mental state, and the current target with distance. A green row with the maneuver name in green marks a stalker AlifeTactics is driving, for the maneuver's whole life. Refreshes twice per second and hides while the PDA is open. Pick a corner to show it.

Records shot outcomes near you: per-rank hit rates split by shooter motion, damage dealt, near misses, and burst lengths per weapon kind, with the driver context (maneuver, Commitment hold, or vanilla) on every record. Tables go to alifetactics_ballistics.log once a minute. Off costs nothing.
Live on-screen readout of the recorder: session length, shots, and per-rank hit rates standing and moving, with damage dealt. Needs the recorder on. Pick a corner to show it.
Restore all AlifeTactics MCM settings to defaults. Use after upgrading from a version with a different MCM structure.
Warning: save or discard pending MCM changes first, otherwise they override the reset on the next Accept.
AlifeTactics: all settings restored to defaults.
